claims.text: The material is a cobalt-free AlCrFeNiSi high-entropy-alloy powder feedstock intended for SLM processing.
Argon should be replaced by helium as the SLM shielding gas.
Helium flow rate and pressure should be systematically optimized.
Helium has higher thermal conductivity than argon.
Using helium will enhance convective heat transfer and heat extraction from the melt pool.
Enhanced heat extraction will produce more uniform cooling and a stabilized solidification front.
Helium-enhanced heat extraction will moderate the cooling rate.
Moderated cooling will reduce thermal gradients and residual-stress buildup.
Moderated cooling will suppress rapid-solidification-induced elemental segregation.
Reduced thermal gradients and segregation will reduce pores and cracks.
Optimized helium processing will reduce residual stress by approximately 20–30% relative to argon-processed AlCrFeNiSi.
Optimized helium processing will decrease compositional segregation relative to argon-processed AlCrFeNiSi.
The reductions in stress, segregation, and defects will increase strength and toughness.
Conventional argon-based SLM of AlCrFeNiSi typically produces significant thermal gradients, segregation, residual stress, and associated defects.
The comparison should hold laser power, scan speed, layer thickness, and build conditions constant at an ambient pressure of about 0.2 MPa.
The hypothesis is restricted to lab-scale specimens within typical SLM energy-density and build-parameter ranges.
Excessive helium-induced cooling may create other microstructural anomalies.
Machine and specimen-geometry scaling can alter the outcome.

The hypothesis is falsified if optimized helium fails to produce statistically significant reductions in residual stress and segregation approaching the specified range, or if it causes defects or degraded mechanical properties.

contradictions.description: The intervention calls for calibration of both helium flow rate and pressure, while the conditions state that ambient pressure remains about 0.2 MPa and that the only change is substitution of the gas.
Only residual stress is predicted to decrease by 20–30%, but the falsification wording can be read as requiring both residual-stress and segregation reductions to approach that quantitative range.
